body: Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 2 defines a community services card as a card issued under regulation 4, eligible in relation to a community services card as eligible within regulation 8, family income as single income or combined married or partnered income except for residential care disability services cases, family credit income as family scheme income including family assistance credit and minimum family tax credit, ordinarily resident in New Zealand excluding unlawful presence and temporary-entry or transit visa status, student and full-time course by reference to education and student allowance instruments, superannuitant and superannuation income, residential care disability services, tenant, social housing, dependent child, child, and tax year.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 4 authorises the Director-General, on application or otherwise, to issue any eligible person with a community services card, recall a card before or after expiry, re-issue a recalled card, or issue a new card to an eligible person before or after expiry or after loss, theft, damage, or destruction.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 4A applies where a person is eligible for a community services card and is also eligible for a SuperGold Card. The Director-General may issue a SuperGold Card bearing a code indicating entitlement to a community services card, whether or not the person already holds a community services card; Part 1, except regulation 7, applies with necessary modifications as if the coded SuperGold Card were a community services card.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 5 requires each issued community services card to have commencement and expiry dates and not be valid before commencement or after expiry. Cards under regulation 8(1)(a), (ab), (b), or (ba) commence on the date the person became eligible to receive the benefit. A card under regulation 8(1)(c) commences 3 months before the application date. A card under regulation 8(1)(d), (e), or (f) commences on the later of 28 days before application and the date the person became eligible. A card under regulation 8(1)(g) commences when the person began receiving residential care disability services funded under the Pae Ora (Healthy Futures) Act 2022. No expiry date may be more than 3 years after commencement.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 8(1) makes a person eligible for a community services card if the person is a beneficiary who has applied for and is entitled to sole parent support, supported living payment, jobseeker support, an emergency benefit granted instead of those benefits, a veteran's pension, a youth payment, a young parent payment, or an accommodation supplement; a person receiving weekly income compensation or weekly compensation under the Veterans' Support Act 2014; a child in respect of whom an orphan's benefit, unsupported child's benefit, or child disability allowance is payable; a tenant of social housing; a person with family credit income at or below the regulation 8(6) amount, 1 or more dependent children, and ordinary residence in New Zealand or family assistance credit entitlement; a person without dependent children whose family income is at or below the regulation 8(5) amount and who meets ordinary residence, age 16 or over, dependent-child, superannuitant, veteran's pension, grandparented-rate spouse or partner, and Veterans' Support compensation exclusions; a superannuitant whose superannuation income is at or below the regulation 8(5A) amount; a student whose family income is at or below the regulation 8(5) amount, is ordinarily resident, and is undertaking a recognised full-time tertiary course; or a person receiving Pae Ora-funded residential care disability services with a financial means assessment under the Residential Care and Disability Support Services Act 2018.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 8(3) makes the spouse or partner of a person eligible for a community services card also eligible if that spouse or partner is ordinarily resident in New Zealand, unless either spouse or partner is receiving residential care disability services funded under the Pae Ora (Healthy Futures) Act 2022. Regulation 8(3A) excludes the spouse or partner of a beneficiary eligible only under regulation 8(1)(a)(vii) for young parent payment unless that beneficiary is a veteran to whom Veterans' Support Act 2014 section 162(1) applies.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 8(4) provides that, for regulation 8, a person is entitled to receive a family assistance credit if the person receives instalments of a family assistance credit under Income Tax Act 2007 subparts MA to MG and MZ for a period commencing on or about the community services card application date, or received a family assistance credit under those subparts in respect of the preceding tax year.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 8(5) sets the appropriate amount of family income at $34,974 per annum for a single person living in shared accommodation, $37,116 per annum for a single person living alone, and $55,501 per annum for a married or partnered person.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 8(5A) sets the appropriate amount of superannuation income for regulation 8(1)(e) at $37,372 per annum for a single person living in shared accommodation, $39,796 per annum for a single person living alone, and $59,694 per annum for a married or partnered person.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 8(6) sets the appropriate amount of family credit income at $67,791 per annum for a 2-person family, $83,444 per annum for a 3-person family, $96,266 per annum for a 4-person family, $108,860 per annum for a 5-person family, and for a family with 6 or more persons $122,724 for the first 6 people plus $12,440 per annum for each additional person.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 8(7) defines family for regulation 8(6) as a group living together in the same household, comprising not less than 1 adult and not more than 2 adults who care for 1 or more dependent children in the group, and the dependent children who are part of the group.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 8(8) defines grandparented rate for regulation 8 as a rate specified in clause 1 of Part 2 of Schedule 1 of the New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001, or the relationship (partner not receiving superannuation or pension) rate specified in regulations referred to in Veterans' Support Act 2014 section 169.

Health Entitlement Cards Regulations 1993 regulation 9 applies Schedule 3 of the Social Security Act 2018, with necessary modifications, when income, net income, or family credit income must be ascertained for assessing community services card eligibility. The Director-General may set the income-period start date up to 2 years before the application date, and computed income, net income, or family credit income is rounded down to a whole dollar.
